Title: Archive search: UI default mode 'default' (and neighbors/output/reasoning/tree) returns HTTP 400

## Metadata Summary
- Priority: 1 (critical)
- Type: bug
- Tags: archive, search, mode, validation
- Estimate: Not specified
- Spent: Not specified
- Remaining: Not specified

## Inheritance
Parent bead: web-kyzr (status: CLOSED)
Inheritance chain: web-kyzr (closed) → web-kyzr.16
No metadata inheritance needed (parent is closed).

## Dependencies
- web-kyzr (parent) — **VERIFIED CLOSED** via `bd show web-kyzr`

## Goal / Description
The Archive Browser Search view is broken by default because the frontend sends a mode value the backend rejects.

Evidence (verified by calling the endpoint):
- webapp/templates/index.html:439-447 defines the search-mode <select> with options: default, neighbors, output, reasoning, tree, timeline, first.
- webapp/static/js/archive-browser.js:20 sets pagination.search.mode = 'default' and loadSearch() (line ~918) sends mode=pg.mode.
- webapp/routes/archive.py api_archive_recall() validates: valid_modes = ('timeline', 'first') and returns 400 otherwise.

Observed responses for GET /api/proxy/archive/recall?model=test-model&query=hello&mode=<m>:
- default   -> 400 Invalid mode: default. Supported modes: ('timeline', 'first')
- neighbors -> 400
- output    -> 400
- reasoning -> 400
- tree      -> 400
- timeline  -> 200
- first     -> 200

Result: clicking Search with the default selection always fails with 'Invalid mode: default'. Selecting any of the four unimplemented modes also fails.

Expected: accept 'default' as an alias for 'timeline' server-side (and either implement or remove/disable the neighbors/output/reasoning/tree options in the UI so the user cannot select an unsupported mode). Add a test asserting mode=default returns 200.

Files: webapp/routes/archive.py (api_archive_recall mode validation), webapp/templates/index.html (search-mode select), webapp/static/js/archive-browser.js (pagination.search.mode default).

Bead: web-yb03
Title: test_archive_server.py module-level patches pollute the pytest session

## Metadata Summary
- Priority: 2 (high)
- Type: bug
- Tags: testing, pytest, patches, pollution
- Estimate: Not specified
- Spent: Not specified
- Remaining: Not specified

## Inheritance
No parent bead (standalone).

## Dependencies
None.

## Goal / Description
PRE-EXISTING bug, NOT caused by the web-mol-6nj.3 archive test refactor (the global patch block predates it).

tests/test_archive_server.py is named test_*.py, so pytest imports it during collection. At module import time it runs:

    for p in patches:
        p.start()

These patches (webapp.models.get_models, webapp.routes.archive._get_model_config, webapp.routes.archive.get_proxy_manager, webapp.routes.status.get_models, webapp.routes.status.get_status_registry, webapp.routes.status._get_model_statuses_parallel, webapp.routes.system.get_hardware_info) are started globally and never stopped. Because the module is imported for collection, the patches leak into the whole test session.

Reproduction:
    python3 -m pytest tests/test_archive_server.py tests/test_routes.py -q
    -> 4 failed (TestStatusRoutes::test_status_returns_unique_model_per_row, TestStatusRoutes::test_status_mnemonic_proxy_per_model, TestUpdateModelMeta::test_status_returns_speculative_decoding_model, TestUpdateModelMeta::test_status_returns_model_path_in_binary_form)

Running tests/test_routes.py alone passes (63 passed). Running the full suite (tests/ minus test_archive_browser.py) shows 7 failures, 5 of which are caused by this pollution (4 in test_routes.py, 1 in test_integration.py::TestRemoteModeIntegration::test_remote_mode_status_endpoint).

Expected: test_archive_server.py should not start global patches at import time. Options: rename it so pytest does not collect it (e.g. archive_test_server.py) and update the subprocess reference in tests/test_archive_browser.py, or move the patch setup into run_server()/a fixture so it only applies when the server actually runs.

Verification: python3 -m pytest tests/ -q --ignore=tests/test_archive_browser.py should not show the test_routes/test_integration failures caused by this module.

Files: tests/test_archive_server.py, tests/test_archive_browser.py (if renamed).

Bead: web-lifn
Title: he() HTML escaper does not escape double quotes (latent XSS in attribute interpolation)

## Metadata Summary
- Priority: 2 (high)
- Type: bug
- Tags: security, xss, escaping, core
- Estimate: Not specified
- Spent: Not specified
- Remaining: Not specified

## Inheritance
No parent bead (standalone).

## Dependencies
None.

## Goal / Description
PRE-EXISTING BUG — not caused by the web-mol-j1k change under review, but discovered during that review.

Location: webapp/static/js/core.js:78-86

The project's central HTML-escaping helper he() contains a no-op replacement for double quotes:

    function he(str) {
      return String(str)
        .replace(/&/g, '&')
        .replace(/</g, '<')
        .replace(/>/g, '>')
        .replace(/\"/g, '"')      // <-- no-op: replaces " with ", should be "
        .replace(/'/g, ''');
    }

Verified: he('a"b<c>&d') returns 'a"b<c>&d' — the double quote is left intact.

Impact: he() is used in ~60 places in ui-controls.js alone and widely across archive-browser.js, chat.js, add-model.js, download-manager.js, etc., frequently interpolated into double-quoted HTML attributes, e.g.:
  - webapp/static/js/ui-controls.js:4317  data-conversation-id="${he(strata.conversation_id)}"  (new code from web-mol-j1k)
  - webapp/static/js/archive-browser.js:624,626,629,839,984,1117  data-conv-id / title attributes
  - webapp/static/js/add-model.js:226, download-manager.js:26  data-* attributes

Any value containing a double quote (conversation titles/previews, model names, filenames, conversation ids) can break out of the attribute and inject markup/handlers — a latent XSS vector. Practical exploitability is low for a local single-user tool, but the escaping helper is fundamentally broken and defeats the intended XSS protection.

Expected fix: change the double-quote replacement to '"' (and add a regression test asserting he('"') === '"').

Files: webapp/static/js/core.js.

## Standard Rules
- Work ONLY on this bead (web-lifn).
- Environment isolation: verify with `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree`; confine ALL modifications to current working directory.
